articles.author: Pratham Gupta
articles.description:
Welcome to Week 3 of the "Demolish the Giant" series. This week, we dive into Meta — the company that bet big on a future in virtual reality but ended up chasing ghosts in a laggy metaverse.
Mark Zuckerberg, a visionary with relentless ambition, plunged Meta into the metaverse era with Oculus and billions in investment. He saw a future where virtual worlds would replace real ones. But dreams don’t always sync with reality — especially when your VR legs feel like spaghetti.
His obsession? Creating a new internet where you live inside the screen, not just look at it.
Meta poured billions into VR hardware, software, and social platforms. They built Horizon Worlds — a VR social network that promised endless possibilities.
But here’s the catch: users stayed skeptical. Technical glitches, lack of content, and a general feeling of awkwardness kept the metaverse niche at best.
Meta’s metaverse was more of a phantom limb than a new reality.
While the metaverse lagged, Meta doubled down on collecting your data. VR headsets track every glance, every gesture, every moment of attention.
Privacy advocates warn that this level of surveillance inside virtual worlds could become the ultimate data trap.
Meta’s real metaverse might be the invasion of your personal space and mind.
With the metaverse hype deflating, Meta is pivoting quietly back to its core: social media and AI.
But the question remains — can a company so invested in a VR dream admit defeat?
Or will Meta keep chasing shadows in virtual worlds while reality moves on?
Meta’s metaverse is a cautionary tale of ambition without timing. A vision that’s more glitch than game changer.
Mark’s dream to live inside the internet faces a harsh reality: the real world still wins — for now.
✨ Coming Next Week: AMAZON — The Invisible Empire
Where convenience meets surveillance and the warehouse meets your doorstep.
Stay vigilant. Stay critical.

Let the demolition continue.
articles.title: 🏗️ DEMOLISH THE GIANT: META — The Metaverse That Never Was

articles.author: Vigneswaran Manivannan
articles.description:
JOINS- A JOIN clause is used to combine rows from two or more tables, based on a related column between them.
***Different Types of Joins

INNER JOIN: Returns records that have matching values in both tables
LEFT JOIN: Returns all records from the left table, and the matched records from the right table
RIGHT JOIN: Returns all records from the right table, and the matched records from the left table
FULL JOIN: Returns all records when there is a match in either left or right table
**
**
select n.name,n.country,s.division,s.gender from new_staff_details n inner join staff_details s on n.name=s.name;
select column1, column2
select n.name,n.country,s.division,s.gender from new_staff_details n left join staff_details s on n.name=s.name;
select column1, column2
select n.name,n.country,s.division,s.gender from new_staff_details n right join staff_details s on n.name=s.name;
select column1, column2
select n.name,n.country,s.division,s.gender from new_staff_details n full join staff_details s on n.name=s.name;
articles.title: JOINS- 19-06-2025
